hint.text:
A sign is a type of hand gesture that represents a certain sound or word.

We are going to be learning right-handed signs, but if you are left-handed, you can mirror them!
hint.label: Signs

atoms.text:
You are about to see some signs. Try to copy them.

You can repeat the exercise as many times as you want!

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: British Sign Language (BSL) is a visual means of communication that uses hand gestures, facial expressions and body language. It is mainly spoken by deaf and hard of hearing people.
atoms.sound: British Sign Language is a visual means of communication that uses hand gestures, facial expressions and body language. It is mainly spoken by deaf and hard of hearing people.

atoms.text: Just like spoken language, there are different sign languages in different countries. For example, American Sign Language (ASL) is spoken in America. Sign languages also have their own grammar, which is different to spoken languages.
atoms.sound: Just like spoken language, there are different sign languages in different countries. For example, American Sign Language is spoken in America. Sign languages also have their own grammar, which is different to spoken languages.

atoms.text: Each word usually has its own sign, but if you don’t know a sign, or want to say a name, you can fingerspell with the sign alphabet.

b: ++A language that uses hand gestures and facial expressions as a means of communication.
A language that people speak aloud as a means of communication.
++No, there are lots of different sign languages.

atoms.a: When can the sign alphabet be used?
b: ++When signing a name or place that does not have an alternative sign.
++When you don’t know a sign and need to spell it out.
Always! Every sign is finger spelt.
